AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to authorizing school
districts to establish an insurance reserve fund in an amount and manner
determined by a qualified and independent actuary certified by the American
Academy of Actuaries to be suitable, reasonable and necessary
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2067

SPONSOR: JORDAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to authorizing
school districts to establish an insurance reserve fund in an amount and
manner determined by a qualified and independent actuary certified by
the American Academy of Actuaries to be suitable, reasonable and neces-
sary

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 6-n of the general municipal law by providing
that any school district may establish insurance reserve funds in
compliance with section 6-n and provisions in the education law.  The
provisions also include a limit on funds reserved to be determined by an
independent actuary.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Current law allows municipal corporations to self-insure to provide
health insurance to their employees, officers, and retirees. Section 6-n
of the general municipal law specifically does so by allowing these
municipal corporations to establish and make expenditures from insurance
reserve funds, but exempts accident and health insurance from these
provisions.

Previous chapters authorized specific school districts to use their
insurance reserve funds for expenses related to health and accident
insurance as defined by paragraph three of subsection (a) of section one
thousand one hundred thirteen of the insurance law. In the era of the
tax cap, several school districts have opted to adopt self-insurance to
manage rising healthcare costs, and for these districts, insurance
reserve funds are necessary to maintain their self-insurance programs.
These districts have requested several bills currently before the legis-
lature that would allow their individual school district to do so, but
the policy of the State should be aimed at allowing all school districts
this degree of flexibility. This bill offers exactly that by expanding
the authorization to any school district that wishes to create or use an
insurance reserve fund for health self-insurance.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Similar to S.7702 of 2018, 3rd Reading

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The first of July next succeeding the date on which it shall have become
law.

thousand one hundred thirteen of the insurance law. In the era of the
tax cap, several school districts have opted to adopt self-insurance to
manage rising healthcare costs, and for these districts, insurance
reserve funds are necessary to maintain their self-insurance programs.
These districts have requested several bills currently before the legis-
lature that would allow their individual school district to do so, but
the policy of the State should be aimed at allowing all school districts
this degree of flexibility. This bill offers exactly that by expanding
the authorization to any school district that wishes to create or use an
insurance reserve fund for health self-insurance.

S.7702 of 2018, 3rd Reading

None to the state.

The first of July next succeeding the date on which it shall have become
